messages:
sara: Heads up — after the kernel-selection change merged yesterday we're seeing a ~18% host CPU uptick on p99 tail for small-chat workloads. Notably most of the extra cycles are in token parse + framing.

mike: Can you paste the pprof/top output? also which model + commit.

sara: Model: gpt-small-v2 (quantized). Commit: 7f3a2b1 (kernel selector rewrite). Quick flame summary:
```
flame%  cumulative   self
20.3%   20.3%       token_parser::parse_bytes
12.1%   32.4%       stream::frame_coalesce
9.8%    42.2%       http2::writev_flush
7.2%    49.4%       kv_cache::lookup_miss_path
```
Heap/allocs look normal. This was during steady QPS ~1200 with avg seq_len 80.

ana: That selector change added an "aggressive mini-batch kernel" path for short sequences, right? IIRC it tries to prefer kernels with lower per-token overhead even if less throughput. Could be increasing preparse/serialize churn.

jeff: If it's picking a different kernel the run-loop could be changing alignment, causing more buffer churn in the host framing layer. Can we repro locally with --mini-batch-hint enabled/disabled?

sara: Repro script I used:
```
./tools/loadtest --model gpt-small-v2 --qps 1200 --avg-seqlen 80 --duration 10m --profile pprof.pb
```
I ran with selector=auto. With selector=legacy (old policy) p99 cpu drops back to baseline.

mike: Two quick checks: 1) batching heuristics counters (mini-batch vs regular) and 2) KV cache hit/miss rate around the same window. If mini-batch increases, we may be doing more tiny writev calls -> http2 overhead.

sara: KV stats for the window (aggregated):
```
kv_hits: 92.1%
kv_misses: 7.9%  (miss penalty: ~1.8ms avg)
mini_batches: 38% of requests
avg_writev_per_request: 3.1 -> previously 1.7
```

ana: avg_writev up from 1.7 to 3.1 is a smoking gun for extra framing calls. That will push HTTP/gRPC syscalls and serialize overhead.

jeff: Could also be tokenization moving host-side due to kernel wanting pretokenized inputs. Check whether pretokenization offload flag flipped.

sara: Checked — pretokenize_offload=false in both runs. Parser time still up.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed 7f3a2b1 to canary (cluster: us-west-2-canary) at 2026-03-20T10:12:03Z :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Rolling back is available: /rollback 7f3a2b1

mike: Quick experiment idea: force kernel selector to prefer legacy for sequences < 128 and rerun. If p99 falls we know it's kernel->host-framing interaction. Also try increasing stream chunk size to reduce writev frequency.

ana: I ran a micro-canary toggling selector policy for short sequences => results (10m runs):
- selector=auto: p99 latency 52ms, host CPU p99 +18%
- selector=legacy: p99 latency 50ms, host CPU baseline
- selector=auto + stream_chunk_bytes=64k: p99 latency 55ms, host CPU +4%

Interpretation: new kernel choice adds host-side churn; increasing chunk size reduces syscalls but adds a small latency/regress tradeoff.

jeff: Sounds like two levers: 1) refine kernel selection cost model to include host framing syscalls (estimate writev count) and 2) adjust batching heuristics so mini-batch is used only when it reduces total host+device cost.

sara: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to augment kernel-selector scoring with an estimated host_cost score: host_cost ~= writev_per_request * syscall_cost + parse_cost. Also adding a flag to cap mini-batch fraction under high qps.

mike: Also add a small telemetry metric: writev_per_request tagged by kernel_choice so we can correlate automatically.

jeff: For the short term we should canary a selector patch + stream_chunk_bytes=64k default for canary cluster. That seems low risk and buys time for selector model adjustments.

sara: I'll push the canary change and a perf dashboard tile showing writev_per_request, mini_batch_fraction, kv_hit_rate, selector_choice. PR in ~30m.

ana: :eyes: will watch the canary graphs once live.

jeff: Nice triage team. If the updated scoring model reduces host parse cycles we can revert chunk size later. :thumbsup:

mike: One follow-up: check gRPC windowing behavior — if many small frames are sent, TCP Nagle interaction could also add tail jitter. Add tcp_info sample for p99 requests.

sara: noted. will capture tcp_info and pprof snapshots in next run. Thanks all.
summary: short investigation thread: kernel-selector change increased host CPU due to more writev/frame churn; plan: refine selector scoring, add telemetry, canary chunk-size increase
